verifiers.name: Spec fixture roundtrip
verifiers.description: A TXTAR fixture under test/spec/ that lowers a query to SQL and, where seeded, executes it against chDB and asserts on the returned rows.
detects: wrong SQL lowering
wrong result rows against a known seed
cannot_detect: semantic drift against the reference backend's own engine

an emit-type mismatch chDB coerces silently (e.g. UInt8/UInt64 -> *float64) but production clickhouse-go's real strict positional scan rejects with a 502 -- chDB is a coercive, not a strict, oracle for this class, so a green roundtrip here says nothing about whether the identical query strict-scans cleanly; only VERIFIER-REAL-CLICKHOUSE-STRICT-SCAN's real-server evidence can show that

verifiers.name: Reference differential
verifiers.description: Runs a query against both cerberus and the real reference backend (Prometheus/Loki/Tempo) over shared seed data and diffs the responses.
detects: semantic drift against the reference backend
cannot_detect: internal plan correctness independent of the final response shape

verifiers.name: Static invariant scan
verifiers.description: A source scan rejecting a forbidden pattern outright (e.g. a caching call site outside the one sanctioned result_cache stamp site).
detects: a forbidden pattern reintroduced at any call site
cannot_detect: a semantically equivalent effect reached through an undetected mechanism

verifiers.name: Go unit test
verifiers.description: A table-driven `go test` asserting a pure Go function's behavior directly (no chDB, no reference stack), run via `just test-unit` (go test -race ./...).
detects: logic errors in the function under test
boundary/edge-case regressions pinned by table-driven cases
cannot_detect: drift against ClickHouse's actual runtime behavior
drift against a reference backend's behavior

verifiers.name: Type-checked lint rule
verifiers.description: A golangci-lint rule (forbidigo, analyze-types: true) that resolves identifiers through Go's type checker rather than matching source text, run as part of the `lint` CI job.
detects: a forbidden symbol used anywhere in the scanned path set, including under an aliased import
cannot_detect: a differently-named accessor that reaches the same forbidden effect through a symbol not on the forbid list
a false-clean result from a local agent-worktree run, which this repo's own record shows can report "No issues found" without genuinely analysing — only a real CI `lint` job run counts as evidence

verifiers.name: Dependency graph lint
verifiers.description: The go-arch-lint tool, which parses .go-arch-lint.yml's declared component/layer graph and fails if an internal/** package is undeclared or imports across a layer boundary the graph forbids, run as part of the `lint` CI job.
detects: an internal/** package missing its component declaration
an import that crosses a forbidden layer boundary
cannot_detect: whether a package's declared layer is the RIGHT layer for what it does — that placement judgment is reviewer discipline
a false-clean result from a local agent-worktree run — only a real CI `lint` job run counts as evidence, per this repo's own operating record

verifiers.name: Property-based oracle differential
verifiers.description: A pgregory.net/rapid property test that draws a randomized or deterministically engineered dataset and query, evaluates the query against both cerberus's real HTTP handler (chDB-backed, full parse/lower/optimize/emit/execute pipeline) and an in-tree oracle, and shrinks any disagreement to a minimal reproducer.
detects: value-level divergence across a wide generated input space
a regression reintroduced into a previously-fixed bug class the generator's dataset specifically engineers for
cannot_detect: divergence in a shape the generator's grammar or dataset pool never draws — each gen/*.go file documents its own deliberate exclusions
drift against a real, separately-started reference server; the oracle here is in-process or hand-written, not the real backend (see VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL for that)

verifiers.name: Documented provenance review
verifiers.description: A hand-maintained provenance record — a doc comment or header file enumerating, entry by entry, which lines of a mixed corpus are copied from a third-party source and which are this repository's own additions — checked by a person reading the corpus against that record, not asserted by any script.
detects: a corpus entry's authorship being misattributed to the wrong source, when a reviewer actually cross-checks the documented list against the corpus file
cannot_detect: a new corpus entry added without updating the documented list — nothing scans for that drift automatically

verifiers.name: Reference status-code differential
verifiers.description: Fetches both cerberus and the real reference backend's raw HTTP response to a fixed, known-invalid request without the 200-only success fold every other differential pass applies, and asserts the two backends' status codes agree. The Loki and Tempo sibling passes (status_parity.go, compatibility/tempo/driver's `-- expect_status --` axis) express "both backends must REJECT this request the same way," which a body-diffing pass that folds every non-200 response into an UnexpectedFailure cannot express.
detects: one backend accepting a request class the other rejects, or vice versa
a shared rejection boundary silently drifting to a different status code on one side
cannot_detect: any answer-level drift for a request both backends accept — that is VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL's job
a rejection-reason mismatch when both sides already return the same status code for different reasons

verifiers.name: Ledger enrollment check
verifiers.description: coverage-package-floor.mjs, the cheap structural half of the coverage gate: it shells out to `go list` and `go tool cover` only (no chDB, no containers, no real test run) to find every package that carries statements in the full build, and fails if any such package has no committed floor file under test/coverage-floor/.
detects: a package with statements missing a coverage-floor ledger entry
a PR that lowers an existing committed floor
cannot_detect: whether a committed floor value is itself high enough to catch a real regression — the floor is a ratchet on the measured value, not an absolute correctness bar

verifiers.name: In-process forked reference evaluator
verifiers.description: Runs a query against the real upstream reference engine in-process, via a documented fork accessor (docs/upstream-forks.md) that supplies engine-internal state the harness computes itself as ordinary data preparation (e.g. nested-set tree numbering) rather than reimplementing the operator semantics under test. No live server is started and no wire/HTTP boundary is crossed — the harness constructs the engine's own internal representation directly and asks the real engine code to evaluate it, then compares identity-aware results (e.g. TraceID/SpanID) against cerberus's own answer.
detects: operator/evaluation-semantics divergence against the exact upstream reference implementation, independent of network or server variance
an identity-level (not merely count-level) mismatch in which specific records matched
cannot_detect: wire-shape or HTTP/gRPC-response-layer divergence — only a live, separately-started reference server (VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL) exercises the actual transport

a defect in the reference engine's own live OUTPUT that contradicts the reference engine's own documented, unit-tested semantics for the identical shape — an in-process match proves only that cerberus agrees with the reference SOURCE CODE, not that either agrees with what a live deployment of that same code actually returns

verifiers.name: Optimizer snapshot pair
verifiers.description: A TXTAR fixture pinning both the pre-optimizer and post-optimizer SQL and chplan-print snapshots for the same input plan (the optimized/unoptimized and chplan_optimized/chplan_unoptimized sections cerberus issue #3335 added, in test/spec/optimizer/ and, as sql_optimized/args_optimized, in every promql/logql/traceql fixture), generated by internal/optimizer's TestOptimizer.
detects: an optimizer rewrite changing the emitted SQL or plan shape in an unreviewed way for the fixture's own case
cannot_detect: two structurally different SQL/chplan pairs that are nonetheless semantically equivalent under ClickHouse's real execution
whether the optimized SQL actually executes to the same result rows as the unoptimized SQL — that is VERIFIER-OPTIMIZER-PROPERTY-EQUIVALENCE's job

verifiers.name: Admission wiring test
verifiers.description: A Go test that mounts a head's real HTTP handler (Mount) — or, for the /tail route, drives an actual WebSocket upgrade and frame exchange — onto a live httptest.Server with a real *admit.Limiter, and observes end-to-end admission behavior (the HTTP status/header or close frame a genuine client receives) rather than testing the Limiter type in isolation.
detects: a head's own mux wiring failing to invoke the limiter it was constructed with
a route mounted on the wrong budget (e.g. /tail drawing on the request budget instead of its own tail budget)
the wrong HTTP status, header, or WebSocket close code reaching a real client on rejection
cannot_detect: a defect in the underlying semaphore's own concurrency guarantees — that is VERIFIER-GO-UNIT-TEST's job against the admit package directly
gRPC transport wiring: this verifier only ever exercises a head's HTTP mux, never a real *grpc.Server

verifiers.name: Real ClickHouse integration test
verifiers.description: An integration-tagged (`//go:build integration`) Go test that dials a real ClickHouse server via testcontainers-go and observes server-side state — connection pool statistics and the server's own native-protocol session census — that no fake, chDB, or mocked substrate can produce, because the behavior under test depends on a live TCP session and clickhouse-go's real driver internals.
detects: whether a pooled ClickHouse connection survives or is destroyed by a given teardown ordering
a real driver/pool regression invisible to chDB (which has no connection pool) or to a fake cursor
cannot_detect: anything about cerberus's own in-process admission semaphore — this verifier never constructs an *admit.Limiter, so it proves nothing about admission-slot recovery, only about the separate ClickHouse connection a request's handler may have held

verifiers.name: Optimizer property equivalence
verifiers.description: A rapid-based property test (internal/optimizer/property_test.go, build-tagged chdb) that generates random plan trees and executes both the unoptimized and Default().Run-optimized forms against an ephemeral chDB session, asserting their row sets are equal.
detects: an optimizer rewrite that changes a query's real result rows for a plan shape the generator can draw
cannot_detect: a semantic drift confined to a chplan node kind the generator's narrow grammar never draws — internal/optimizer/property_coverage_test.go's uncoveredOptimizerKinds ledger names the current gaps
chDB-vs-real-ClickHouse execution drift: chDB is a coercive, not a strict, oracle for type mismatches production ClickHouse would reject

verifiers.name: chDB handler roundtrip
verifiers.description: A Go test that seeds a deterministic fixture into a real embedded ClickHouse (chDB) session, mounts a head's real HTTP handler (Mount) onto httptest.Server, issues a genuine HTTP request, and asserts on the DECODED WIRE RESPONSE — the full parse/lower/optimize/emit/execute/render pipeline, not a hand-built comparison string, a stubbed querier, or an internal plan/SQL snapshot.
detects: wrong resource- or attribute-scope projection reaching the real wire response
a schema override (a custom table or column name) the handler fails to honor end to end
cannot_detect: semantic drift against the reference backend's own engine — chDB is cerberus's own embedded ClickHouse, not a reference implementation (see VERIFIER-REFERENCE-DIFFERENTIAL)
production-cluster-only behavior (a real clickhouse-go connection, cluster-specific settings) — see VERIFIER-REAL-CLICKHOUSE-INTEGRATION

verifiers.name: Real ClickHouse strict-scan differential
verifiers.description: An integration-tagged (`//go:build integration`) Go test that runs the pinned golden SQL corpus, the router-corpus write+read seams, the optcorpus query_log-predicate and exit_status-enum reconciliation arms, the non-matrix Loki/Prometheus metadata endpoints, the histogram real-exporter-schema differential, the route-A/route-B same-query differential, and the perf-smoke sentinel differential against a real ClickHouse (testcontainers) through the production strict-scan client path, run via the required `strict-scan` CI lane's named recipes (e.g. `just strict-scan-test`, `just router-corpus-integration`).
detects: an emit-type mismatch chDB coerces silently (UInt8/UInt64 -> *float64) but production clickhouse-go strict-scans and 502s on
a system.query_log.type predicate naming a non-member that ClickHouse coerces to String and silently matches nothing
a deployed exit_status Enum8 narrower than the member set the binary writes, which a no-op CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves undetected until a real batch insert rejects it
a metadata/label-values endpoint decoder bug that bypasses engine.QueryPlan entirely and so has no chDB-backed fixture corpus of its own
a native exp-histogram quantile/columnar-decode/classic-bucket-discovery regression against the REAL upstream clickhouseexporter table shapes
cannot_detect: Tempo search-row decoder bugs (cerberus issue #1635, which needs a hidden pipeline stage to reproduce and is not yet covered by any strict-scan recipe)
rows that scan successfully but return the WRONG value — that is Layer 6a-c's (chDB roundtrip) job, not strict-scan's

verifiers.name: Deterministic cursor-teardown-order test
verifiers.description: A plain (untagged) Go test that drives a real HTTP handler seam through httptest with a fake streaming cursor recording ordering/timing, pinning that the handler closes the cursor before cancelling its query context and that the close completes within a bounded drain budget — deterministic, in-process, no chDB and no real ClickHouse, runs in the required `check` lane.
detects: a refactor that hoists a context cancel ahead of the streaming cursor's Close (the ordering the handler must never reverse)
a teardown that never returns once its context has died, silently pinning a pool slot for as long as ClickHouse takes to finish streaming an abandoned result set
cannot_detect: whether a real pooled ClickHouse connection actually survives or is destroyed by a given ordering — the fake cursor here cannot model clickhouse-go's two terminal branches (drain-to-EndOfStream on a live context releases the connection; cancel-then-close destroys the socket outright); only a real driver against a real server can, which is VERIFIER-REAL-CLICKHOUSE-INTEGRATION's job

verifiers.name: Deterministic stubbed-querier chaos injection
verifiers.description: A Go test that injects a fault — a stubbed ClickHouse connection drop, a mid-stream cursor fault, a panic mid-handler, or a goroutine-leak assertion via goleak.VerifyNone after driving requests through a real httptest.Server — against a STUBBED querier rather than a real ClickHouse. Deterministic, in-process, runs in the required `check` lane. Proves the LOGIC of a resilience contract; VERIFIER-LIVE-STACK-CHAOS-INJECTION proves the same contract holds against a real deployment under real faults.
detects: a circuit-breaker state-machine defect (CLOSED->OPEN threshold, OPEN backoff, HALF-OPEN probe outcome, concurrent-probe admission)
a leaked goroutine on the happy path, an error path, a concurrent-request burst, or a route-memo retry
a handler panic that fails to release an already-acquired admission slot or otherwise crashes the process instead of recovering
cannot_detect: whether the SAME contract holds against a real ClickHouse outage, a real network partition, or real pod-kill timing — those failure MECHANISMS cannot be manufactured against a stub; only VERIFIER-LIVE-STACK-CHAOS-INJECTION exercises them
goleak's own ignore-list excludes known persistent runtime goroutines (e.g. Go's HTTP idle-connection cleaner); a leak that happens to match one of those signatures is not caught

verifiers.name: Live k3d-stack chaos injection
verifiers.description: kubectl- and HTTP-driven fault injection (`.github/scripts/chaos-run.mjs`) against a real k3d cluster (cerberus + ClickHouse + Grafana + OTel collector, `just e2e-up`) with real NetworkPolicy/pod-kill manifests under `test/e2e/chaos/manifests/`, asserting the landed resilience contracts hold under REAL faults rather than a stubbed querier. Runs as the `chaos` job in `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`, informational: push-to-main + nightly + manual dispatch only, never a PR gate and never in release.yml's RELEASE_REQUIRED_CHECKS.
detects: the circuit breaker actually opening/closing end to end under a real CH pod-kill, with the documented 502-then-503 ordering and /readyz behavior
a per-query wall-clock timeout actually returning a breaker-neutral 503 under a real slow query
replica failover actually keeping the Service serving from a survivor
a real NetworkPolicy partition driving the same breaker-OPEN end state (gated on a runtime kube-router enforcement probe; recorded not-applicable rather than a vacuous pass when the probe fails)
admission+pool saturation shedding cleanly under real burst concurrency
the route-memo route-B retry actually firing against a real ClickHouse MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
cannot_detect: a single green run cannot by itself distinguish a scenario whose precondition genuinely didn't materialise this run from one whose precondition has permanently stopped materialising — that requires the separate weekly chaos-not-applicable-rate.mjs audit across MULTIPLE runs, not this verifier's own per-run evidence

handler-panic recovery is only a passive end-of-run health gate here (all three heads 200 after the fault storm), not a dedicated scenario — VERIFIER-DETERMINISTIC-CHAOS-INJECTION is what actually pins that contract

verifiers.name: Consumer-corpus request replay
verifiers.description: Replays a captured REAL Grafana request shape (test/consumer-corpus/grafana-<version>/*.json, with provenance and per-entry expectations) against cerberus's in-process HTTP handlers and decodes the response EXACTLY as the consumer decodes it — strict gogo/protobuf unmarshal into tempopb types for Tempo, bare logproto-shaped JSON for Loki, Prom API envelopes for Prometheus. Two lanes share one corpus: the default-tag lane (runs in the required `check` lane) backs handlers with canned-row stubs and pins routing/status/decodability; the `chdb`-tagged lane (runs in the chdb workflow's `probe` job via `just test-chdb`) executes the full parse->lower->optimize->emit->chDB pipeline over small seeds and additionally evaluates each entry's data predicates.
detects: a wire-envelope-shape regression of exactly the incident class the 2026-06 week found only through the e2e browser stack (a bare Trace served where Grafana strict-decodes a TraceByIDResponse envelope, an enveloped detected_fields where Grafana reads top-level fields, a missing spanSets, a drilldown 422 on a nil groupBy)
a data-bearing predicate regression across the full pipeline for a real consumer request shape (chdb-tagged lane only)
a route-memo retry that silently changes the wire shape a consumer decodes, even though the retry succeeds
cannot_detect: a consumer request shape Grafana has never been observed to send — the corpus is a snapshot, and Layer 9's e2e crawler and drilldown specs are the corpus MINERS; this verifier only replays what has already been captured

large-cardinality, production-scale data volumes — corpus seeds are small by design, so a cardinality/fan-out regression that only manifests at scale is VERIFIER-RESOURCE-FANOUT-BOUND-TEST's or Layer 12's job, not this one's

verifiers.name: Concurrent-dispatch resource/fan-out bound test
verifiers.description: A plain Go test exercising internal/chclient's data-shard fan-out gate (a semaphore bounding how many concurrent ClickHouse dispatches one query may hold open at once) against a fake driver, asserting the allocation floor (DataShardCount<=1 never allocates), the concurrency cap under real goroutine racing, the cancel-then-kill-before-release ordering, and idempotent release. Deterministic, in-process, runs in the required `check` lane.
detects: a change that makes the gate allocate for DataShardCount<=1 (the documented zero-behavior-change guarantee for every deployment that predates the field, cerberus issue #3081/#3128)
concurrent dispatch exceeding the configured cap under real goroutine racing
a cancelled dispatch releasing its slot WITHOUT first issuing KILL QUERY, which would leave an abandoned query still consuming server resources
a double-release double-killing the same query
cannot_detect: whether a REAL ClickHouse server actually honors the KILL QUERY this gate issues on a cancelled dispatch and frees its own resources promptly — proven only against a fake driver.Conn here, and no real-clickhouse-substrate binding for this specific claim exists today (tracked as cerberus issue #3489, filed rather than silently widened into an existing binding's claim)

SQL-plan-level compute fan-out — peak intermediate rows versus leaf scan rows inside ONE dispatch (Layer 12's cardinality/scale-wall ratchets, test/perf/cardinality_ratchet_test.go and scale_wall_pin_chdb_test.go) is a completely different axis from this gate's concurrent-DISPATCH-COUNT bound; a deployment can satisfy one while violating the other

verifiers.name: Migration-tier substrate and parity scenario
verifiers.description: A build-tagged (`migration_tier1` / `migration_tier2`) Go test driving a real docker-compose tier stack (pinned reference Prometheus/Loki/Tempo beside ClickHouse + an OTel collector + cerberus, or that stack plus a query-only external ruler for Tier 2) with a deterministic all-signal fixture, asserting `cerberus migrate verify` reports zero diverge-count against an INDEPENDENTLY REBUILT oracle on each side (never one side against the other), and, for Tier 2, that a real fired alert reaches a dead-end webhook receiver. Runs via `.github/workflows/migration-e2e.yml`'s `migration.e2e` lane, gated behind the `migration_tier1`/`migration_tier2` build tags so the required `check` lane's untagged `go test ./...` never reaches for Docker.
detects: ingest-bridge type-reconstruction bugs (what the OTel collector writes versus what the reference backend itself stored)
schema/label/histogram fidelity loss across the write seam
a migrate-verify comparator bug, via the negative control that deliberately perturbs one side and asserts the harness reports the disagreement
alert-firing divergence that query-level parity alone cannot see (Tier 2 only)
cannot_detect: a lowering or emitter bug that the eight seeded archetypes never happen to shape a query into — it surfaces here, if at all, as an opaque parity diff rather than a located defect; Layers 1-13 own actually pinpointing it
any customer topology beyond the eight seeded archetypes, or anything docs/migration-testing.md section 6.4 records as a declared scope limit

verifiers.name: Real-ClickHouse performance-baseline regression gate
verifiers.description: An integration-tagged Go test that loads a real, trimmed production data sample into a real ClickHouse and asserts each pinned sentinel's max-of-5 peak memory (and expected HTTP outcome) against a committed baseline plus an absolute cap-relative ceiling, run via the `perf-nightly` lane (`go test -tags=integration -run TestPerfNightlyRealCH ./test/perf/nightly/...`).
detects: a peak-memory regression, for the EXACT pinned sentinel shapes, past the committed baseline or the absolute ceiling
an HTTP outcome (success/rejection) changing for a pinned sentinel at its calibrated scale
cannot_detect: general algorithmic correctness or asymptotic boundedness for a query shape, data volume, or ClickHouse/cerberus version combination the committed baseline never measured — a green result is MEASURED evidence for the exact pinned sentinel/version combination, not a semantic proof of general correctness; a new shape needs its own sentinel and a version bump needs its own re-measurement
wall-clock regressions — those are performance.benchmark's (benchstat, manual dispatch, advisory even at release) job, not this gate's

verifiers.name: SQL-plan cardinality / fan-out ratchet
verifiers.description: A chdb-tagged Go test in the `perf-guards` job (chdb.perf-guards lane, substrate chdb, required on the release gate) that pins a fixture's PEAK INTERMEDIATE CARDINALITY, structural fan-out flags (an unbounded CrossJoin, an arrayJoin feeding a JOIN, an uncapped WITH RECURSIVE, a correlated subquery), and recursion depth against a committed baseline (test/perf/cardinality-baseline/<head>/<name>.json, scale-wall-baseline.json), failing on an upward regression, a newly-tripped structural flag, or deeper recursion; a decrease never blocks, and the ceiling only tightens on a deliberate `just update-golden cardinality`. Complements the static internal/perf/fanout lint, which flags a structurally-unbounded shape on every corpus fixture's lowered plan and emitted SQL with no chDB execution at all.
detects: an upward fan-factor regression (peak intermediate rows / leaf scan rows) against the committed per-fixture baseline
super-linear wall-time scaling against a swept parameter for a known-hot construct
a deeper recursion depth than the committed baseline records
a fixture whose fan-out shard was never recorded, closing the 'unrecorded fixture -> red perf-guards on main' failure mode
cannot_detect: a fan-out in a construct nobody wrote a static rule or a baseline fixture for — the corpus-wide nightly profiler (test/perf/profile, the perf-profile workflow / performance.profile lane) is the wide net for that residual class: it is release-required (release.yml's RELEASE_REQUIRED_CHECKS names `profile`) but absent from the live main-branch PR ruleset, so an ordinary PR can merge without it having run even once

the concurrent-DISPATCH-COUNT bound internal/chclient's data-shard fan-out gate enforces — this verifier bounds ROW CARDINALITY inside one dispatch, a different axis than VERIFIER-RESOURCE-FANOUT-BOUND-TEST's concurrent-dispatch cap; a fixture can satisfy one while violating the other
